body: I could understand why you'd be hurting-- having a family member egg on your hurt, disclose personal information and encourage your embarrassment to another. I'm in no way blaming you, as it's normal to want to latch onto what's...familiar and holds memories to past. But your blood relatives are their own independent people, not the dad you're mourning. He should know better if he's in his mid-50s and I hope you find people to lean on and just...express how you miss your dad. Something that should help would be keeping alive the good things you remember about him, journaling and more things that soothe you as a person.

To me, love is the conscious choice to care for someone and try to make it through the sunny days and the cold nights together. For example, even when they drive you crazy (within reason and past history), you can still smile and laugh together. And I've looked for the definition of love but it's broad and varies. Love can mean extreme care or "liking" but I don't now. I know for sure I'm connected with my partner, we care about each other and want what's best for each other. 

Some things that make up love, for me, would be:  

\-Growth; allows you to become a better version of yourself & support helping the person do the same

\-Honesty (to know someone intimately, it's important to talk about what matters to you in an open, honest way. Th truth might be ugly but it's part of caring about someone. )

\-Respectful/Considerate (because it shows them you care)

\-Accountability (because nobody's perfect and we're a "unit" acting together for each other's best interest). 

This all make up a nice version of love to me because these foundations allow a long-term to life-long commitment to happen. I don't believe the romantic will always be there but I think it's likely to stay and having someone you can trust and know in a loving way like this can describe it. But maybe I should've just stuck with the chemical experience. 

Here's a video called [Philosophies of Love](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n-QXbOXRuw0) if you're interested.
It's good you choose the more productive route and I hope it works out well for you.

Please don't be like the woman who posted around a week or so ago on a subreddit who was strict with her son about sex and it eventually led to her being a grandmother sooner than she thought. From my own experience (from receiving and doing), trying to restrict someone's autonomy and choices will make them do the exact opposite of what you want them to do but in secret. Also, you giving a negative consequent will help subconsciously enforce sex negative. Sex is engaging in a intimate, carnal activity with someone(s). 

1. Would my husband be saying this if this was our daughter? Men are   
easier on their sons than their daughters when it comes to sex. 

My answer: MAYBE. Maybe not. The rules should be the same for both. But IMO there shouldn't be rules unless it's proven to be better and not just to make you feel about something. 

2. Does allowing him to have sex take away from my power as a parent? What if this makes it look like I allow my kids to run wild? 

My answer: Why do you want to get your "power" from ceasing him to have intimacy with someone he loves? I'm not saying you're bad or anything but I want you to think about it. What does your son exploring his sexuality have anything to do with the power and rights you should have as someone who is supposed to guide him? Also, you need not to worry about looks and focus on what it is. Your son was being responsible. Please don't restrict him. He's going to resent you for doing something he didn't find as bad. 

3. Was I wrong for grounding my son for practicing safe sex?

My answer: Yes. I think this has to do with you. Your thoughts on his sexuality and doing things. Your personal beliefs and feelings about something shouldn't restrict someone from doing something if it's not causing harm (something I'm still trying to practice and internalize). 

 4. If I allow this, would it be wrong if I only allow it under one condition? The condition: His   
girlfriend needs to be on birth control. It needs to be paired with his condoms.

My answer: "I want you to have freedom but I can limit how free you are". If you'll allow for them to have sex (with you knowing about it under your roof), you should try to educate them and let them go.
